listenings.text: Good afternoon everyone, here are the results of the junior final. In first place, with a total of sixteen point four, from right here on this beach: Toby Nguyen. Toby was a rookie last season and today he is the champion. The runner-up is Marcus Hill, with fifteen point one. It was a close final and both scores were excellent. The prize giving is at four o'clock, next to the tower. And one quick note: yesterday's delay was our fault, not the ocean's, and we are sorry about that.

So that was my weekend. Friday was horrible. We were at the beach at seven and the ocean was completely flat. We were there for five hours and nothing happened. My mum was furious, my brother was bored, and I was cold. Then Saturday came. The conditions were unbelievable, the crowd was huge, and my first heat was at half past seven. I wasn't nervous, which was strange. I was third in my heat, so I am out, but honestly it was the best day of the season.

reading.rtitle: One flat Friday, one perfect Saturday
paras: Last April the junior contest was almost a disaster. On Friday the conditions were terrible. The ocean was flat, there was no swell at all, and the organisers were nervous. Nobody wanted to cancel, so at nine o'clock they announced a delay. At midday they were still waiting. Some parents were angry, and two families were already on the road home.

On Saturday everything was different. The swell was three metres, the wind was offshore, and the beach was full. The draw was on the wall at six in the morning and the first heats were in the water by seven.

The final was between a local rookie and last year's champion. The rookie was fifteen years old and it was his first contest. He wasn't the favourite, but at the end he was the winner. The champion was the runner-up, and he was the first person to shake his hand.
The prize was small, only a board and two hundred dollars, but the photo of those two on the sand was on the front page of every surf site the next morning.
